summary: Kemo Jin was a scholar of Indology, Sinology, and linguistics. He held posts at Visva-Bharati University (1941–1945) and Peking University, where he became Professor of Sanskrit in 1948.

Ken McLeod works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned an M.Sc. at the University of British Columbia, studied with Kalu Rinpoche and other traditional teachers, was resident teacher at Kagyu Dongak Chuling (~1985–1990), and founded Unfettered Mind (1990).
Kendall Marchman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied under Mario Poceski and earned a PhD from the University of Florida in 2015.

Kengo Harimoto works in Indology and philosophy. Educated at Nagasaki, Kyushu, and the University of Pennsylvania (PhD 1999 under Wilhelm Halbfass), he held posts at Hamburg, Mahidol, and Naples "L'Orientale", among others.

Kenichi Kuranishi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held an associate professorship at Taisho University (attested 2013–2026) and was a research fellow at the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).
Kenji Ishii specializes in religious studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1973–1985) and held a post at Kokugakuin University around 1990.
Kenji Kinugawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1972–1982) under Yoshitaka Iriya and Seizan Yanagida.
Kenji Matsuo works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1974–1984) and held a post at Yamagata University (~1989–2020).
Kenji Shimada was a scholar of Sinology, philosophy, and history. He studied at Kyoto University (~1938–1941) and served as a researcher there (~1952–1981).

Kenji Takahashi is an Indologist who studied at Leiden University as an exchange PhD student under Peter C. Bisschop and completed his doctorate under Diwakar Acharya and Yuko Yokochi. He held a fellowship at the University of Naples Federico II (2019–2021).
Kenji Watanabe specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Jozef Deleu and held an assistant post at the University of Tokyo (attested 1978).
Kenjiu Kasawara was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Oxford from 1879, training under Friedrich Max Müller (1879–1882) and Arthur Anthony Macdonell.
Kenjuro Yanagida was a philosopher who studied at Yokohama National University and under Kitaro Nishida (~1920–1924). He held an academic post at Hirosaki University.
Kenkai Naganuma was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology. He held posts at Kyushu University (~1926–1946) as professor emeritus and at Kurume University.
Kennard Lipman specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed doctoral studies under Herbert V. Guenther and worked as a sessional instructor at the University of Calgary.
Kenneth Doo Young Lee works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He completed his doctoral studies under Ryuichi Abe at Columbia University and held a post at Stetson University (attested 2007).

Kenneth G. Zysk is an Indologist and historian who earned an M.A. at UC Santa Barbara and a Ph.D. at Australian National University. He held positions at Eastern Michigan University, the University of Copenhagen, and several other institutions.

Kenneth J. Guest works in religious studies and Sinology. Educated at Columbia, Peking University, Union Theological Seminary, and the CUNY Graduate Center (PhD), he has held posts at Hunter College and Baruch College.

Kenneth J. Saunders was a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied under W. D. C. Wagiswara. He served as Professor of the History of Religion at Pacific School of Religion (~1921–1935) and lectured at the University of California (~1921–1934).

Kenneth K. Inada was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He was a professor at the University at Buffalo (attested 1983–1999) and chaired both Bukkyo Dendo Kyokai (until 1999) and the Numata Center (1996–1999).
